In RobustPrune (Algorithm 2), once p* is added to N_out(p), a candidate p′ is removed from the candidate set V if:

**α · d(p*, p′) ≤ d(p, p′)** (page 4)

In words, p′ is pruned when it is closer to p* by at least a factor of α than it is to p. Here α ≥ 1 is the distance threshold (page 4).

Some context from the same page:
- The loop repeatedly picks p* = arg min over p′ ∈ V of d(p, p′), the closest remaining candidate to p, and adds it to N_out(p) (page 4).
- Before the pruning step, the procedure stops if |N_out(p)| = R, the degree bound (page 4).
- Using α > 1 means the distance to the query shrinks by a multiplicative factor of α at each node on the search path. With the SNG property it only decreases (page 4). The SNG rule is the α = 1 case, which removes p′ when d(p, p′) > d(p*, p′) (page 3).
